title: Developer-first hosted API: positioning, activation copy, and pricing experiments
content:
Objective:
Short praxisable playbook to: 1) unify developer-facing value props for Hosted API, 2) provide a set of quickstart and onboarding copy variants optimized for activation, and 3) propose concise pricing language + experiment ideas that minimize confusion and highlight predictable unit economics.

Context:
We continue to hear two threads from trial users and early PLG signups: (a) devs love how fast they can get a model running, but trip over uncertainty about unit cost and latency guarantees; (b) platform teams ask for a clear path from prototype (hosted) to dedicated/private without rewriting code. This doc is meant to be a working draft with concrete microcopy and experiment hypotheses for the next two sprints.

Audience segments (primary):
- Product engineers / full-stack devs: want fast iteration, sample code, and predictable costs for prototypes.
- ML engineers / infra: care about throughput, KV cache, and model versioning—want visibility into latencies and per-call economics.
- Platform / security leads (mid-market & enterprise): want migration path, SLAs, and private deployment options.

Core positioning pillars (tight messaging):
1) Developer-first: "Code-first API, production-ready defaults" — ship prototypes in minutes, ship to production without rewriting.
2) Predictable unit economics: "Clear per-token & per-embedding math" — examples that translate usage into dollars.
3) Production-grade performance: "Latency SLOs and intelligent fallbacks" — built for live product traffic.
4) One API, multiple modes: "Hosted now, Dedicated/Private later" — same interface for all deployment modes.

Short elevator lines (variants to A/B test):
- 1-line hero options:
  A: "Hosted LLM inference that scales from prototype to production — predictable latency, predictable cost."
  B: "Ship LLM features fast. Keep latency low, costs transparent, and the option to move on‑prem when you need it."
  C: "A developer-first API for real-world LLM performance and unit economics."

- 2-line subhead variants (pair with A/B hero):
  - "Start with free credits and a 5-min quickstart. When you’re ready, pin model versions and reserve capacity with a single config change."
  - "Streaming, function calls, and SDKs with production defaults — no ops team required to start."

Quickstart copy snippets (for onboarding emails, banner, CLI):
- Email subject: "Start your first Redwood API call in 5 minutes — free credits inside"
- Onboarding banner: "Try the API: 3 lines of code, one endpoint, instant streaming. Example in your language."
- CLI snippet blurb: "Paste this into your terminal and get a streamed response back in under a second: [example]."

Code sample shorthand (one-sentence guidance for docs):
- "Use the SDK’s quickstart to send a prompt, enable streaming in one flag, and view per-request cost in the Console."

Pricing-language drafts (goal: clarity + concrete examples):
- Headline: "Pay for what you use — transparent per-token and per-embedding rates."
- Supporting sentence: "We charge by token generation and embeddings; the Console shows a live cost estimate before you send a request."

Pricing example vignettes to include on pricing page (microcopy + math):
- Prototype scenario (Frontend dev): "A chat prototype that generates ~2k tokens/day = ~120k tokens/month. At $0.003/1k tokens this is ~$0.36/month — start free with credits."
- Production bot (SaaS app): "10k active users, median 200 tokens/session => 2M tokens/day ~ 60M tokens/month => example monthly spend of $180 at $0.003/1k tokens (plus embedding costs)."
- Embedding lookup example: "1M vectors at 1536 dims stored externally; embedding cost = X per 1k vectors (show simple math)."

Guidelines for pricing copy: keep the math front-and-center, use plain language for 'per-token' vs 'per-request', and include a 'cost calculator' link as primary CTA. Avoid ambiguous words like 'credits' without showing conversion to USD.

Common objections and rebuttals (sales/SDR cheat sheet):
- Objection: "I’m worried about runaway costs."
  Rebuttal: "We give per-request cost previews, usage alerts, and quota limits you can set. Plus, try with free credits to estimate your footprint."
- Objection: "How do I move to Dedicated or Private later?"
  Rebuttal: "Same API surface. Deployment mode is a control-plane change; we provide migration runbook and support."
- Objection: "Latency spikes under load."
  Rebuttal: "Built-in autoscaling, intelligent routing, and cheaper high-throughput model variants. We publish model latency profiles in the Console."

Competitive differentiation bullets (short):
- Versus cloud provider managed endpoints: "Developer ergonomics + model catalog curated for inference profiles; clear unit economics."
- Versus LLM API-only players: "Production controls (rollouts, tracing, cost breakdown) and a migration path to Dedicated/Private."
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: "No infra burden to start, and an escape hatch to move on-prem with consistent API."

Experiment ideas (A/B tests & analytics to run):
1) Hero copy A/B: "Predictable cost" vs "Ship fast" — measure signup -> first API call conversion.
2) Pricing page: show example scenarios vs raw unit table — measure time on page and estimate conversions.
3) Onboarding microcopy: add a per-request cost preview in quickstart vs no preview — measure retention after 1st week.
4) Free credits messaging: show 'USD-equivalent' vs 'credit points' in emails — measure trial activation and spend.

Metrics to track for success:
- Activation: % signups that make first API call within 24h
- Cost clarity: % users who view cost calculator before first paid call
- Retention: 7-day call retention and conversion to paid usage
- Sales enablement: Average time from inbound demo request to POC kickoff (should shrink with clearer migration messaging)

Copy examples for CTAs and banners:
- CTA short: "Start generating — free credits"
- CTA neutral: "Estimate your cost"
- Enterprise CTA: "Talk to sales about Dedicated capacity"

Next steps (practical):
- Align with product: confirm per-token price points + embedding rates to use in examples (owner: Liam).
- Design: create two hero variants and pricing vignette artwork for experiment.
- Engineering: wire a lightweight cost preview into the quickstart flow (Jira: GTMP-482).
- Content: build a 90s video showing "from zero to first API call" with CTA to cost calculator.

Open questions (for leadership/product):
- Should we standardize on USD-only examples or show local currencies for EMEA/APAC pages?
- Do we expose 'burst' pricing for hosted vs a flat estimate?
- What is the default model we put in the quickstart (lowest-latency or highest-quality)?

Appendix: sample email flows (short)
- Day 0 (welcome): "Welcome — your account has free credits. Run this 1-line example to see a live response and cost preview."
- Day 2 (activation nudge): "Hint: enable streaming to reduce latency and cost for X use cases. See example."
- Day 7 (conversion nudge): "Your trial shows potential: here’s an estimated monthly cost at X usage — get 10% off first month if you commit to Dedicated by date."

Notes and provenance:
This doc synthesizes conversations with Solutions Eng (Zoe), Product Hosted API (Liam), and early trial telemetry from Jan–Feb 2025. Intend to iterate after two experiments (hero A/B and pricing vignette) and produce final messaging for next marketing campaign.

End of draft.
